desc:
Two non-negative integers are stored in singly linked lists, one decimal digit per node, most significant digit first (the head holds the leading digit). Each list is passed as an array of digits from head to tail. Neither number has leading zeros, except that the number 0 itself is [0].

Return the sum as a list of digits in the same encoding, again without leading zeros. For example a = [7,2,4,3] and b = [5,6,4] represent 7243 and 564, and the answer is [7,8,0,7].

The numbers can have thousands of digits, so do not convert them to machine integers. Solve it without reversing the input lists if you can.
constraints: No leading zeros (except for the number 0 itself)
hints: Addition starts at the least significant digit, which is at the end of both lists, and the lists may have different lengths.
Either push the digits of each list on a stack, or align the lists by their lengths. With stacks the last digits come off first, exactly in the order addition needs.

Pop one digit from each stack (use 0 when a stack is empty) plus the carry, create a node for sum % 10 and put it in front of the result built so far. Keep going while any stack has digits or the carry is non-zero.
editorial: Do ordinary column addition from the right. A stack per list turns the front-to-back lists into back-to-front streams. Repeatedly pop a digit from each non-empty stack, add the carry, and prepend a new node with total % 10 to the answer list; the carry becomes total // 10. Prepending a node is O(1) on a singly linked list, so the answer comes out already in most-significant-first order.

Finish when both stacks are empty and no carry is left (a final carry creates a new leading 1). Time O(n + m), space O(n + m) for the stacks. A stack-free variant first finds the lengths, then recursively adds the aligned digits and handles the carry on the way back.
